MEMBERSHIP BENEFITS

Some benefits are available in certain branches as a percentage off ales, food and other items. We also have a national members benefit. Please remember to carry your SPBW membership card and ask about discounts. NB: Discounts may change or cease.
NATIONAL MEMBERSHIP BENEFITS

GET 'er BREWED

Although an online supplier of home brew kits and equipment, providing a next day delivery service for just £4.75, they do however, have a stockist at Hillstown Farmshop, Ahoghill. There is a wide variety of home brew kits and equipment available there. They have basic information on wine & beer brewing onsite.

Hillstown Farmshop & Kitchen 128 Glebe Road Randlestown Antrim BT41 3DT Telephone 0800 2289 433 Use our SPBW code for 5% discount on brewing equipment and materials. Thank you Jonathon.

RED LETTER DAYS

Red Letter Days offers experience gifts for all tastes, from adrenaline-charged driving experience gifts to high-flying hot air balloon gifts. If you're looking for a memorable present they'll never forget, you've come to the right place. Choose from an impressive range of experience days, including gourmet dining experiences and cooking classes for the foodie in your life. Mark any occasion and whether you're seeking a gift experience for a loved one, family, or a colleague, Red Letter Days are guaranteed to have just the present you're looking for. Browse our site for inspiration and buy them something they'll really love.

Use our SPBW code for 15% on Red Letter Days offers! Thank you Gemma.

ADP PHOTOGRAPHY

Prints, Commissions, Handfastings, Bespoke Portraiture (Pets included) I am based in Leeds, in the West Riding of Yorkshire. My work, like me, evolves and changes depending on my moods. I like the isolation and starkness of a lone tree in winter, to reflections on a calm lake in summer. I am a strong supporter of SPBW and good ales. Please feel free to browse the galleries, and should you have any questions or comments drop me an email. All images on the site are available for purchase as high-quality (mounted/unmounted) prints, or as downloadable images for your personal use. All prints are limited to 25, each being numbered and signed. Use our SPBW code for 15% discount on products. Thank you Alan

CANAL CRUISING

WHY NOT TRY ONE OF OUR CANAL HOLIDAYS IN THE UK? Welcome to canal boat holidays with Canal Cruising, a family business for over 68 years. The best way to enjoy the amazing canals of England and Wales from your own floating home. SPBW discount can be used against a weekend, midweek or a weeks holiday on any boat at any time of the season. Use our SPBW code for 10% on cruises. Thank you Karen

ALES BY MAIL

Ales By Mail was created to champion the amazing beers produced by the craft breweries of the world, which offer so much more than the industrialised beers that dominate supermarket shelves today.

Ales By Mail is for everyone, whether you are already a beer lover, looking for something new, or searching for a unique gift for friends or family, we have built this store to give you all the information you need to make an informed purchase. Use our SPBW code for 10% on Ales By Mail beers. Thank you.

SPBWNI MEMBERSHIP BENEFITS

GET 'er BREWED

Although an online supplier of home brew kits and equipment, providing a next day delivery service for just £4.75, they do however, have a stockist at Hillstown Farmshop, Ahoghill. There is a wide variety of home brew kits and equipment available there. They have basic information on wine & beer brewing onsite. Hillstown Farmshop & Kitchen 128 Glebe Road Randlestown Antrim BT41 3DT Telephone 0800 2289 433 Use our SPBW code for 5% discount on brewing equipment and materials. Thank you Jonathon.

SUNFLOWER PUB

This used to be the old Tavern bar, famed for being about the last of the Belfast pubs to have a security gate at the front door, harking back to the 70's era. As such it had been the frontage for some films shot for that era. It has now been refurbished, still with the familiar exterior design, but still holding on to an old fashioned backstreet and unpretentious bar atmosphere - something sadly missing in the city. The owner, Pedro, has been in the trade a long time and serves a great selection of bottled beers and has a cask ale pump on the counter. The bar has a tiled floor with half-height wood paneled walls and painted brick and a quirky barber's chair. The stairs, with 60's style pop-art painted walls and old wood floor, leads to the upstairs live music room complete with a a very unusual bar counter. Sunflower Pub 65 Union Street Belfast BT1 2JG (028) 9023 2474 (T) Thank you Pedro.

THE HOUSE OF HOMEBREW

Established in 1978 and everything under one roof to make the perfect brew. Stock includes Young, Munton's, Tom Caxton, Woodforde's, Cooper's and Geordie. Wine kits include Californian Connoisseur, Vinamat, Carafe etc. I bought some kits here and the staff have always been helpful and friendly. 305 Upper Newtownards Road Belfast, County Antrim BT4 3JH Thank you Paul.

THE HUDSON BAR

Originally DuBarry's, it is now a bit more upmarket but still into music. A three story building with large lettered windows downstairs overlooking a sad Smithfield. Small tiled and wood floor with a distressed mirror behind the small bar. Bric-a-brac, painted bricks and old fashioned wallpaper set the scene. Two floors upstairs for music and events. To the rear is the smoke area, which has been fully opened up as an alfrsco lounge area, and is actually the old arcade taken over, giving a huge potential for parties, events, BBQs. There is a good selection of bottled beers and draught from the Williams Brothers - though this is keg. This includes a badged Hudson Beer. The staff are knowledgeable and friendly. 10-14 Gresham Street Belfast BT1 1JN (028) 9023 2320 (T) Thank you guys.

HILDEN BREWERY

Well known for its Real Ale Festivals in the 80's, the brewery is set in Georgian stables and comprises of the Tap Room Bar (the only bar in Ireland to serve draft real ale exclusively), a restaurant and a visitor centre. It is the longest lasting independant brewery in Ireland. Hilden House Hilden Lisburn BT27 4TY Tel: (028) 9266 0800 (brewery) Fax: (028) 9260 3511 Thanks to everyone.

MOLLY's YARD

The restored stables of College Green House off Botanic Avenue are now home to Molly's Yard restaurant. Opened in late December 2005, Molly's Yard is already a favourite haunt of South Belfast residents and Staff at the university. Molly's Yard 1 College Green Mews Botanic Avenue Belfast BT7 1LW Tel: (028) 9032 2600 Thank you all at Molly's Yard.

SALTY DOG

A revamped hotel/restaurant in Bangor now making a name for itself with craft beers, "Meet The Brewer" nights and now "Tap Thursday" for cask ales. Salty Dog 10-12 Seacliff Road Bangor Co.Down BT20 Tel: (028) 9127 0696 Thanks to Ken and everyone at the Salty Dog.

ERRIGLE INN

One of Belfast's favourite and busiests bar/restaurants. Now into a growing selection of good quality caks ales and looking to move into more. The food is excellent and the staff are great. Errigle Inn 312-320 Ormeau Road Belfast BT7 2GE Tel: (028) 9064 1410 Thank you Paul and all the staff.

BEER FROM THE WOOD IS AVAILABLE

We have been advised that Ye Olde Mitre, 1 Ely Court, Hatton Garden, EC1N 6SJ are serving three, Three Kings Brewery, North Shields beers from wooden barrels. Whilst stocks last!

The Evening Star in Brighton served two beers direct from wooden barrels Sunday 30th May 2021.    Beak Oopla 10% Coffee and Vanilla Imperial Stout and Dark Star 'Critical Mass'.   They also had Tosta, a pop up kitchen selling Portuguese toasted cheese sandwiches for the day.

There have been BfTW on the 1st and 2nd Mondays of the month at 'Ye Olde Mitre', 1 Ely Court, Hatton Garden, EC1N 6SJ, coinciding with regular Campden Hill Branch and NEC meetings. This is on hold thanks to the virus, lockdowns etc. Will hopefully return to business as usual when the pub reopens.

There have been BfTW on the last Mondays of the month at the Blyth Hill Tavern, 319 Stanstead Road, Forest Hill, SE23 1JB, coinciding with regular Cobra Cow meetings. This is served from a pin kindly bought by Con for the pub. Will hopefully be business as usual when pub reopens.

First Beer from the Wood Launch - Saturday 31st October 2020 - Evening Star, 55/56 Surrey Street, Brighton, BN1 3PB. One beer served from pin recently bought by the manager.

Beer from the Wood festival - Thursday 10th - 13th September 2020 - The Lord Harrowby, Grantham, Lincolnshire. 8 -10 bftw were expected to be served, but the landlord, John Senior, had difficulties with some breweries supplying at the time.

Summerfest 2020 - Thursday 27th - Monday 31st August 2020 - Royal British Legion, Marlow. I unfortunately don't remember or noted what bftw they had, but they were excellent as usual, probably why I don't remember. Attended by several local SPBW members plus those from London and other parts of the country.

Redemption Fellowship from the Wood - Wednesday 4th March 2020 - Was served from 6pm at the 'Harp', 47 Chandos Place, London, WC2.

Three Sods Smoked Brown Ale from the Wood - Wednesday 19th February 2020 - Was served from 6pm at the 'Harp', 47 Chandos Place, London, WC2.

Manchester Beer and Cider Festival = Wednesday 22nd-Saturday 25th January 2020 - Manchester Central Complex. The Wood Bar served 73 real ales and sold out by 4pm on the Saturday. A fantastic success. A few SPBW members manned the bar and the SPBW stand. Some others came as customers. A great time was had by all.

SPBW London pub of year 2019 presentation - Monday 13th January 2020 - Ye Olde Mitre, 1 Ely Court, Hatton Garden, EC1. The award was presented to Judith and her staff. Bftw were Windsor and Eton Mandarin and Seattle Porter. The event was very well attended and a good time was had by everyone.

56th Anniversary Event - Sunday 8th December - Ye Olde Mitre, 1 Ely Court, Hatton Garden, EC1 6SJ. Our regular celebration of the founding of SPBW. We had the whole pub to ourselves.  There was Isabella Brown from Park brewery both in metal and from the wood. Judith produced a high-quality buffet with carvery food and was much enjoyed. More then 20 people attended this.

Winterfest 2019 - Thursday 12th - Sunday 15th December 2019 - Royal British Legion, Marlow. Club President John Wilkinson and Bar Manager Andy Shephard, both SPBW stalwarts, ran another very successful festival. The following Bftw included Chiltern Brewery 300's Old Ale 4.9% and Festive Foxtrot 3..9% (Xmas Special), Leighton Buzzard Brewery Bedfordshire Best 4.1%, Stardust Brewery Spiced Slow Roast 4.6% and Animal (XT Brewery) Rook 4.6%. All were very good.

Five Points Brickfields Brown from the Wood - Wednesday 11th December 2019 - Was served from 6PM at the 'Harp', 47 Chandos Place, London WC2.

56th Anniversary Event - Sunday 8th December 2019 - Ye Olde Mitre, 1 Ely Court, Hatton Garden, EC1. It was attended by over 20 people who enjoyed the food and a bftw from Park Brewery.

Five Points London Porter from the Wood - Wednesday 4th December 2019 - Was served from 6PM at the 'Harp', 47 Chandos Place, London WC2.

Pig and Porter Green Hop Dubbel Percy Percy from the Wood - Wednesday 13th November 2019 - Was served from 6PM at the 'Harp', 47 Chandos Place, London WC2.

42nd Norwich Beer and Cider Festival - Monday 21st - Saturday 26th October 2019 - The Halls, Norwich, NR3 1AU. Had 37 Beers from the Wood in St. Andrew's Hall.

Calderdale Beer and Cider Festival - Thursday 26th - Saturday 28th September 2019 - Viaduct Theatre, D Mill, Dean Clough, Halifax, HA3 5AX. Had 19 Beers from the Wood.

Signature Brewery Nightliner Coffee Porter from the Wood - Wednesday 25th September 2019 - Was served from 4pm at the 'Harp', 47 Chandos Place, Covent Garden, WC2. It sold out within 2 hours.

Cannock Chase Beer and Cider Festival - Thursday 19th - Saturday 21st September 2019 - Prince of Wales Theatre, Church Street, Cannock WS11 1DE. Had 4 Beers From The Wood.

Beer Festival - Saturday 24th August 2019 - Royal British Legion, Marlow. The club is situated next door to the Marlow terminus of the Maidenhead to Marlow branch line. Doors are open at 11. There was some beer from the wood available including from Chiltern Brewery.

East London Brewery Quadrant Oatmeal Stout from the Wood - Wednesday 7th August 2019 - From 5PM at the 'Harp', 47 Chandos Place, London WC2.

Three Kings Brewery Shieldsman from the wood - Wednesday 24th July 2019 - From 4PM at the 'Harp' 47 Chandos Place, London WC2.

BMAD

CAMPDEN HILL

This is the first and longest established branch in SPBW. It was founded in 1965 at the Windsor Castle, Campden Hill Road, Kensington, London. Hence the name. The pub was the Branch's HQ for several years afterwards, although we have changed meeting places several times since.    The branch has always had a variety of events like Branch meals, Memorial dinners and walks, Awayday trips out of London, a Not the Christmas meal and even a darts competition as well as pub crawls.   The branch has produced many members of the SPBW NEC over the years including Chairman, Vice Chairman, Treasurer and Secretary. This tradition continues to this day.   Our members are friendly people and we don't bite!  

CASKTORES OF REAL ALE (CRA), Argentina

This year we will have a new edition of our real ale festival, it will be on May 20 and 21, 2022.
 RAND FESTIVAL 4 EDITION

CENTRAL LONDON

Thursday 16th January 2020 - A walk of some of Andy's Old Favourites in WC1.

Walk of some of Andy's Old Favourites

Tuesday 18th February 2020 - Patrick's walk of the Oxford Street, W1 area.

The Three Tuns, Portman Mews South was a cosy Greene King pub with the usual suspects, not too bad for GK. Next Devonshire Arms, 7 Duke Street, a spacious pub with new wood interior with no cash transactions. Trendy hipster beer. Then Angel in the Fields, 37 Thayer Street, a classic Sam Smith's pub, OBB from the wood, usual fine wooden interior, no music, just the sound of conversation. Finally Lamb and Flag, 24 James Street, a Grade II listed building GK pub with the usual suspects and 3 changing beers. Very traditional.

The branch hasn't had any events since then because of the average age of the members. The branch social organiser will let us know when they will start having their Pub Evaluation and Memorial walks as soon as it is feasible.

COBRA-COW

The branch managed to have 2 meetings before the lockdown in March. Then it had it's next social in July at the usual venue, the Blyth Hill Tavern, SE23. 8 people attended plus 3 more Zoomed in from Norfolk, East Sussex and North London. There were 4 beers on at the pub. More meetings happened after that until London went Tier 2.

COLAPS

The Coast of Lancashire Ale Preservation Society (COLAPS) meets on the first Wednesday of every month at The Grasshopper micropub Hillside, Southport. We have a programme of guest speakers at our meetings and regular socials/pub crawls. SPBW members are welcome at meetings and on the socials. For further details please contact Andrew at grasshopperhillside@gmail.com.

CHESASPEAKE BAY

Our only American branch.

COMMON AND ALDBRICKHAM

Common and Aldbrickham branch will hold its first Founders Day outing aka Pete Smith Memorial Pub Crawl on Saturday 19th February. This will take the form of a tour of the pubs of Banbury. An itinerary will be circulated to branch members and other interested parties nearer the time. All SPBW members are welcome to join us. Contact John Dearing for further information: john@jbdearing.co.uk/

Glamorgan and Gwent Branch

Inaugural meeting upstairs at the Flute and Tankard, Thursday 14th October 2021 at 8.00 PM. Do you like beer and would like to meet others who share the same interests and trips out and social gatherings in a friendly and non political atmosphere? We are forming a new branch for people local to Glamorgan and Gwent. Come along to the meeting and learn more about us. All welcome.

Greater Manchester Branch

Since our recent visit to The Flying Horse in Rochdale they have brought their own wooden barrels.

KINGSTON

Some members enjoyed the annual SPBW Beer and Curry (or Bagel) in February. The last meeting before lockdown was in March at the Willoughby Arms, Kingston as usual. We have met regularly since using video conferencing and this included a pub quiz on the 22nd April. Since then there has been another quiz, a sit down comedy night and discussion of favourite admired person, building, record album, book, film etc. Once restrictions were lifted a bit we cycled to local parks to meet with each other with socially distanced beers. After pubs reopening we went to the Sussex Arms, Twickenham to celebrate a member's birthday. In July and August we cycled to the Bell in East Molesey (Greene King but with decent guests), Rifleman, Twickenham (operated by Twickenham Fine Ales) and Woodies Bar, New Malden. Later in August was a Surbiton pub crawl starting off at the Lamb which had an open sided "marquee" with divided into sections. The Black Lion opposite was full of people watching football and given a miss. Then couldn't get into the Coronation Hall, so ended up in the Victoria. A Youngs Pub Company pub and it was well managed that day and had the most customer-friendly service of the evening. St Austells Proper Job was consumed there. Lastly that month, a few members visitied the Marlow RBL's beer festival. Beers were served to distanced tables in a very large function hall. The Rifleman and Lamb were revisited in September and October. Our branch meetings took place at the Willoughby in August, September and October. The latter was noted for the last orders bell being rung at 10pm, the first time any of us had heard such a sound in that venue.

NORFOLKSOAKS

It held a virtual meeting on 2nd April, the minutes of which are no less bizarre then those of the actual ones. Our HQ, the Fat Cat (the original one) has been performing sterling social work through the 'beer hatch'. They also constructed ten tables for external enjoyment until it reopened. It was announced as the CAMRA's Norwich pub of the year. Congratulations to Colin Keatley and his team.

NORTH EAST

Due to the pandemic there wasn't much activity until a social in early July at the Heaton Tap. It was great to see the members again.

NORTH IRISH SEA

After the pubs reopened in late June, branch members made a gluttonous start with dining at three venues on the first day at the Barbary Coast, Creg Na Baa and the Shore in Gansey to comply with all the rules! There has been one new cask pub, the Blind Pig, a return to cask for the community owned Pinewood Estate social club and a new beer Triumph from Okells. The pubs have since been fully open with no restrictions since compared with the whole of Europe. The pub stock has remained relatively intact with about 4% losses. The new brewery Odin's beers have sold spectacularly thanks to the shortage of guest beers on the island. Hooded Ram brewery has now closed. We have been very busy rediscovering outlets on the island including Manx Legion, Peel Legion (sells Manx Cider), yacht clubs, and the Buffs Club in Ramsey. Run by the Royal Antediluvian Order of the Buffaloes, started in 1822 in the Harp Tavern, opposite Drury Lane Theatre.

RACS

Have been holding monthly meetings on Zoom. Attendance has been good and conversations lively. Traditionally the branch doesn't have a formal meeting in August usually because of beer festivals, but that was different this time round. In September, we decided to review the situation about having live meetings for 20 or more people. So far all our members have remained safe, but looking forward to a "real" meeting before long.

ST FORBADIL

Forbadillians always look forward to the annual trip to Tower Brewery in Burton upon Trent on the 4th March and we weren't disappointed. As in previous years we were royally treated by the master brewer John Mills. He is an engaging host and he allowed an open bar with 4 beers on. After an entertaining and informative tour of the historic building, there was a generous fish and chip supper provided for everyone. Planned visits to several beer festivals after that were cancelled thanks to COVID. After the end of the lockdown Fordbadillians continued to visit their local hostelries in the towns and villages of Staffordshire, but we have not met as a group at the Bitter Suite in Lichfield since the new pandemic restrictions came into force.

TYNE AND WEAR

The branch visited Theakstons and Black Sheep breweries in early March. A great day and we managed to catch up with Master Cooper Alastair Simms for a couple of pints in the Black Sheep brewery tap room. A wander and a meal around Masham followed, ending with an overnight stay at the King's Head just off the main square.

WANTZ

We managed to get in a couple of events before the great lockdown. At the end of February we had a pub walk in Temple, WC2, visiting 4 pubs. Starting at the Devereux, Devereux Court. The latter takes its name from Robert Devereux, Earl of Essex and a famous parliamentary general in the Civil War; his bust adorns the facade. A limited selection of beers and rather busy with an after-work crowd. Almost next door is the Edgar Wallace, Essex Street. This is a friendly and cosy free house and we relaxed in the upstairs room. Castle Rock Pale and Crouch Vale Brewer's Gold were our choices among several on offer. The pub is decorated with an abundance of vintage adverts and the shelves are lined with the works of the eponymous author. Another short hop took us to the Cheshire Cheese (Not Ye Olde!). This is an undistinguished Shepherd Neame pub with only one cask beer available, Whitstable Pale Ale with the other pumpclip turned round. We then finished at the Temple Brew House back in Essex Street, a basement bar which offered a fair range of cask and keg beers brewed on the premises. We then made a return visit to Mangal1, just off Stoke Newington High Street, N16. Excellent Turkish food cooked over a large open flame grill. Pre-dinner drinks were at the Farr's School of Dancing on Dalston Lane, on of the Antic chain. Five handpumps offered beers from Volden (Antic's own brewery), as well as Five Points and Thornbridge Jaipur, a temptation we couldn't resist. After the national lockdown, we managed to meet in our usual venues in August and September, but new COVID regulations ruled our an October meeting. When we had visited the Chesham Arms in August there was a distinct lack of real ale. That is until Joe, the friendly manager, took pity on us and cracked open a cask of Five Points Pale that was due to go on the following day. Naturally we took full advantage!

WEST RIDING

A trip to Whitby to visit the Whitby Brewery Tap among others.
